item.title: Pydantic Deep Agents: Open‑Source, Self‑Hosted AI Assistant and Framework
item.description:
Pydantic Deep Agents: Open‑Source, Self‑Hosted AI Assistant and Framework

Pydantic Deep Agents releases an open‑source terminal AI assistant and Python framework. It lets you point any model—Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model—to the same harness.

🔍 Overview

Pydantic Deep Agents is an open‑source, self‑hosted terminal AI assistant and Python framework. It lets you point any model—Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model—to the same harness.

🧩 How it works

  • The assistant runs on Pydantic AI.
  • It can plan, edit files, run shell commands, search the web, remember across sessions, spawn sub‑agents, and connect to MCP servers.
  • The single function call create_deep_agent() provides a model with a filesystem, shell, planning, memory, sub‑agents, sandboxed execution, MCP, and unlimited context.
  • Live Run Forking splits a single run into parallel branches; an AI judge merges the branches back together.
  • When an agent faces a decision point (e.g. “should I refactor this with a decorator or a context manager?” ), the fork‑and‑merge mechanism allows exploring both options.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Type safety 100 % type‑safe
License MIT for the assistant and framework; Apache‑2.0 for Agenticos
Model support Claude, GPT, Gemini, local
Runtime Self‑hosted terminal AI assistant
Harness Same code used for the single‑function create_deep_agent()

🚀 Availability

  • Install it locally and point it at any model.
  • Use it today, or ship your own agent in one function call.
  • The repo contains both the terminal assistant and the Python framework.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a unified, open‑source alternative to commercial assistants like Claude Code.
  • Enables teams to use a sovereign, self‑hosted AI layer with budgets, approvals, guardrails, and activity tracking via Agenticos by Vstorm.
  • The fork‑and‑merge runtime supports parallel reasoning paths, giving developers more flexibility when designing agent behavior.

item.title: React Chat Interface for Pydantic AI Documentation Assistant
item.description:
React Chat Interface for Pydantic AI Documentation Assistant

A new React‑based chat interface for Pydantic AI has been released, powering the documentation assistant at ai.pydantic.dev/web/.

🔍 Overview

  • React chat UI built with Vercel AI SDK.
  • Connects to Pydantic AI’s streaming chat API.
  • Used as documentation assistant.

🧩 Features

  • Streaming message responses with reasoning display.
  • Collapsible visualization of tool call input and output.
  • Conversation persistence via IndexedDB, with migration from legacy localStorage.
  • Dynamic model and tool selection.
  • Dark and light theme support.
  • Mobile‑responsive sidebar.

⚙️ Configuration

  • Startup configuration must be set before the UI module script runs when served below a same‑origin path prefix.
  • basePath controls conversation URLs and browser navigation.
  • apiPath points to the directory containing configure and chat endpoints, independent of basePath.
  • Both accept same‑origin paths and are normalized with a trailing slash.
  • If not set, basePath defaults to the normalized Vite base (offline and CDN builds use /) and apiPath defaults to /api/.
  • Configuration works when a server injects the script into the single‑file offline artifact at request time; the artifact does not need to be rebuilt.
Parameter Default when unset Role
basePath normalized Vite base (/ for offline/CDN) Controls conversation URLs and navigation
apiPath /api/ Directory for configure and chat endpoints

🚀 Development & Availability

  • Install dependencies with pnpm install.
  • Start the Python backend: pnpm run dev:server (requires agent/ setup).
  • Start the Vite dev server: pnpm run dev.
  • Released under the MIT License.

#React #Pydantic #AI #VercelSDK
